thread:
maya: Heads up — planning a schema migration for console route_metrics this weekend. goal is to normalize usage_windows JSONB into columns (window_start, window_end, tokens_in, tokens_out) and add a small tenant_id denorm to speed dashboard joins. doing a dual-write + read-gate rollout. 
ryan: can you paste the migration plan? worried about long-running queries and index bloat.
tanya: dashboards will need the new columns for p99/time-window aggregations. will the api change? we can't break existing saved charts.
jessica: cost/backfill note: previous backfill of route_events ~6h on staging instance. need estimate for tokens -> tokens_in/out split. also need to quota the backfill so it doesn't spike DB CPU.
sam: proposal: dual-write for 3 weeks, with a read-side feature flag (route_metrics_v2) + a lightweight materialized view for console routes that ships only the fields the UI uses. fallback policy if read_gate fails.
maya: plan rough steps:
1) add columns nullable + new indexes (concurrent)
2) dual-write at API layer (hosted + dedicated) behind feature flag
3) shadow backfill job that writes v2 rows without flipping reads (throttle)
4) small canary for 1% of tenants on dashboards (read_gate)
5) monitor query latency and p99 on console (10m windows), flip gradually
6) drop JSONB after 8 weeks once confidence achieved
ryan: what about our existing route-aggregates view that joins route_metrics -> route_profiles? it assumes JSONB path. we'll need a compat adapter or a view rewrite.
maya: yes — add a compatibility view route_metrics_compat as a SQL shim that projects JSONB shape from the normalized columns. kept for queries that still use JSON path. sample shim:
```sql
create view route_metrics_compat as
select id, tenant_id, jsonb_build_object('windows', jsonb_agg(jsonb_build_object('start', window_start, 'end', window_end, 'in', tokens_in, 'out', tokens_out))) as payload
from route_metrics_v2 group by id, tenant_id;
```
ryan: ok that helps for adhoc queries, but console's p99 dashboards run against materialized aggregates. we should add a background job to incrementally populate aggregates from v2 to avoid re-scanning full history.
tanya: for saved charts: we'll add a server-side translation layer that accepts the old queries and rewrites predicates to use the new columns when read_gate is on. this keeps UI unchanged.
jessica: backfill throttling: recommend token-slice approach -> process X tokens/sec per shard. budget estimate: ~200k rows/hr on staging config; prod will be ~10x. i can run a smoke run on prod-like instance tomorrow.
sam: rollout flags list:
- feature.route_metrics_dualwrite (write both shapes)
- feature.route_metrics_readv2 (reads from v2 shim when enabled)
- feature.route_metrics_backfill_running (blocks concurrent backfills)
ci-bot: deploy scheduled: migrations-service -> canaries on staging at 2024-05-22T02:00Z, prod window 2024-05-25T04:00Z. see: https://ci.internal/redwood/deploy/54521
maya: monitoring: add these dashboards before flip:
- route_metrics.write_latency p50/p95/p99
- console.query_p99 (by route and tenant)
- backfill.cpu_utilization and db_locks_count
- error rate for route_metrics_readv2 translation layer
ryan: how will this affect quota calc? quotas read the JSONB tokens totals every minute. we'll need to ensure the quota service reads from v2 or the compat view.
maya: quota-team sync: we'll post an RFC update and tag them. plan is to have quota service read from compat view for a safe ~2-week overlap, then switch to v2 API.
tanya: we should add an audit log for rows migrated (id, old_payload_hash, new_row_id) so we can reconcile counts. also helpful for customer support rollbacks.
jessica: agree. include a reconciliation job that compares tokens sums pre/post per-tenant and surfaces >1% drift.
sam: deployment checklist stub on the runbook: 
- run concurrent index creates
- enable dual-write in small canary
- kick off shadow backfill with throttling
- enable readv2 for 1% tenants, monitor 24h
- increase to 10%, 50%, 100% with checks at each step
- start grace period then schedule JSONB drop
maya: thanks team. i'll post the RFC draft later today and assign owners for backfill + translation layer. ping me if you want to be on the canary rotation. :rocket:
ryan: thanks, will review RFC. :thumbsup:
